key_insight: An evaluator-guided evolutionary loop using large language models can discover quantum circuit designs that outperform the state of the art in both gate count and qubit use.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a practical route to co-design quantum algorithms and reversible implementations, especially for resource-constrained quantum hardware.
method: LLMs propose candidate quantum circuits and architectures.
An independent evaluator checks correctness and scores resource cost.
Search iterates across diverse tasks to optimize Toffoli and qubit counts.
evidence_signal: Across eight benchmark tasks spanning computation, chemistry, optimization, simulation, and number theory, the discovered circuits improved resource trade-offs in seven cases and introduced a new modular inversion architecture in the eighth.
watch_item: The gains depend on evaluator quality and task-specific verification, so translation to larger or noisier hardware settings may require additional validation.
paper_title: Discovering state-of-the-art quantum circuits with large language models
